title: Two Coworkers Talk About Planning a Class Reunion
script: Dewi: [excited] Fajar, guess what? Someone from my old high school class wants to organize a reunion this year.
Fajar: That sounds fun. How many years has it been since you all graduated?
Dewi: [thoughtful] Almost twelve years now. I honestly haven't seen most of them since we finished school.
Fajar: Are you nervous about seeing everyone again after so long?
Dewi: [nervous] A little, actually. People change so much, and I worry we won't have much to talk about.
Fajar: [reassuring] I felt the same before my own reunion last year. It was easier than I expected, honestly.
Dewi: Really? What helped it feel easier once you were there?
Fajar: [warmly] Once the first few minutes passed, old jokes came back, and it felt like no time had passed at all.
Dewi: That's reassuring to hear. I guess some connections just don't fully disappear.
Fajar: Exactly. Shared memories create a bond that doesn't need constant contact to survive.
Dewi: Did anyone surprise you, like someone completely different from who you remembered?
Fajar: [amused] One classmate used to be extremely shy, and now he runs his own small restaurant confidently.
Dewi: That's wonderful. I wonder who will surprise me the most at mine.
Fajar: You'll find out soon. When is the reunion happening exactly?
Dewi: [organized] Next month, at a restaurant near our old school. I'm helping organize the guest list.
Fajar: Do you need any help with planning? I'm pretty good with spreadsheets and lists.
Dewi: [grateful] Actually, yes. I'm struggling to track who has confirmed and who hasn't replied yet.
Fajar: Send me the list tonight. I'll organize it properly for you by tomorrow morning.
Dewi: [relieved] Thank you so much, Fajar. This whole thing feels less overwhelming already.
Fajar: That's what coworkers are for. Now go enjoy reconnecting with your old classmates.
